notes_list.title: Furan and Thiophene — Aromaticity
notes_list.basic_overview: Five-membered heteroaromatic rings contain two double bonds and one heteroatom lone pair participating in the aromatic π system, giving 6π electrons.
notes_list.extra_info_content: One lone pair participates in the π system; another remains in-plane. Electrophilic substitution generally occurs readily at the 2-position.
notes_list.examples: Furan, thiophene and substituted derivatives undergo EAS, with relative reactivity influenced by heteroatom properties and substituents.
notes_list.conditions_and_medium: Mild EAS conditions are often used because these rings can be more reactive than benzene toward electrophiles.
notes_list.mechanism_steps: Electrophile attacks the electron-rich ring to form a resonance-stabilized σ-complex, followed by deprotonation to restore aromaticity.
notes_list.kinetics_and_energy: Rate depends on ring electron density and electrophile strength; harsh Lewis-acid conditions can cause decomposition/polymerization.
notes_list.common_traps: Do not count both heteroatom lone pairs toward aromaticity.

exam_focus.level: IIT-JAM / MSc entrance / GATE concept depth
